liebermann.description_de: British Museum Cotton Otho B XI
liebermann.shelfmark_as_given: London, British Library, Cotton MS Otho B.xi
liebermann.notes: Partly burnt; it once held the Old English Bede from Southwick, the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle (printed by Wheloc; Lambarde's 1564 transcript is now in Dublin) and bishop lists to 1005/12. The remains (c. 1010), bound out of order, contain Alfred–Ine (rubrics and fragments), where Ot is close to E and seems copied from it, and also near l; and II Æthelstan 7–25 (cf. osq).

entries.text_de:
British Museum Cotton Otho B XI, theilweise verbrannt, enthielt einst die Angelsächsische Bæda-Übersetzung aus Southwick stammend5 und die Ann. Anglosaxonici6, nach denen Wheloc druckte, und Lambarde 1564 eine jetzt zu Dublin befindliche Abschrift7 fertigte, ferner Bischofslisten bis 1005/12. Die Reste von Ot, um 1010, enthalten, in falscher Ordnung gebunden, f. 49 Af-Ine Rubriken bis Rubr. Ine 9; f. 50 Af 40—43; f. 52 f. Ine 66—76, 2, u. S. 16. 72. 118; für Af-Ine steht Ot nahe zu E, ja scheint daraus copirt; vgl. Af 42, 7*.

Die Hs. steht in Af-Ine auch nahe zu l.

F. 48. 51 II As 7—25, u. S. 154; vgl. osq.
entries.text_en:
British Museum Cotton Otho B XI, partly burnt, once contained the Anglo-Saxon translation of Bede, originating from Southwick5, and the Ann. Anglosaxonici6, from which Wheloc printed and of which Lambarde in 1564 made a transcript now at Dublin7, and also lists of bishops to 1005/12. The remains of Ot, c. 1010, bound in the wrong order, contain f. 49 Af-Ine rubrics as far as rubric Ine 9; f. 50 Af 40—43; f. 52 f. Ine 66—76, 2, below, pp. 16. 72. 118; for Af-Ine Ot stands close to E, indeed seems copied from it; cf. Af 42, 7*.

The MS also stands close to l in Af-Ine.

F. 48. 51 II As 7—25, below, p. 154; cf. osq.

notes.text_de: Wanley in Hickes’ Thes. ling. sept. III 219. Dass die Hs. Winchester entstamme, wie Turk Code of Aelfred 12 meint, ist unwahrscheinlich, da die Reihe dortiger Bischöfe erst hinter Rochester und Essex folgt.
notes.text_en: Wanley in Hickes’ Thes. ling. sept. III 219. That the MS comes from Winchester, as Turk, Code of Aelfred 12, thinks, is improbable, since the series of bishops of that see follows only after Rochester and Essex.

notes.text_de: Plummer Saxon chron. I p. xiii; II p. xxviii hält sie für copirt aus E.
notes.text_en: Plummer, Saxon chron. I p. xiii; II p. xxviii, considers them copied from E.

wormald.wormald_heading: 1 (ii) BL, Cotton MS Otho B.xi + BL, Additional MS 43703
wormald.shelfmark: London, British Library, Cotton MS Otho B.xi (with the detached king-list leaf now BL, Additional MS 34652, f. 2)
wormald.wormald_date: Bede mid-tenth century; main assemblage (Chronicle, lists, law-book and the rest) 1001×1012, since the Chronicle ends at 1001 and the episcopal lists were extended by another hand to 1012×1013; the Æthelstan code in a third hand possibly of the time of those additions (pp. 172–3). Table 4.1: 1001x1015 (p. 164).
wormald.wormald_origin: Winchester: the Bede scribe also wrote the Parker annals ‘925’–946/55, and the Chronicle, lists and law-book were probably copied from the Parker MS (p. 173; Table 4.1, p. 164); copied soon after 1001, perhaps for Ælfheah’s successor at Winchester when Ælfheah took the Parker MS to Canterbury in 1006 — a guess Wormald flags as unsupported (p. 180). Wanley says it came from St Mary’s Southwick (p. 180 n. 75). Badly damaged in the Cotton fire (p. 173); its last items destroyed in 1731 (p. 178). Basis of Whelock’s editio princeps of the Chronicle (p. 174, n. 42 cont.). Wormald argues episcopal, not lay, ownership (p. 181).
wormald.laws: II As (Grately) in a third scribe’s hand on leaves ruled for 22 lines, placed between the episcopal lists and Af–Ine: on Wormald’s reading a complete but variant text ending at II As 25:2, lacking the Sunday-trading clause and the final perjury clause II As 26 (pp. 176–8). Af–Ine, copied from the Parker MS but with the line lost at Af 1:2 restored (probably by correction) (pp. 174–5). Ymb Æwbricas, a short text on adultery added straight after Ine’s last law (pp. 175–6). Only two leaves of II As and three of Af–Ine survive (p. 173). V As and Iudex were NOT in Otho (p. 176).
wormald.other_contents: Old English Bede (mid-tenth century), completed by the main scribe with Bede’s autobiographical ending; Anglo-Saxon Chronicle (G for Chronicle editors, Plummer’s A) to 1001 with prefatory West Saxon genealogical king-list (leaf now Add. 34652, f. 2); papal and episcopal lists; then, after the laws, the Burghal Hidage, the poem ‘Seasons of Fasting’, and medical recipes (mostly also in Bald’s Leechbook, an MS written by the scribe of the Parker ‘925’ annals and the Otho Bede). Once 231 leaves; under a quarter survive. The lost parts are known from Nowell’s transcript (Add. 43703) and Wanley’s description and annotations (Bodleian, Gough London 54) (pp. 172–80).
wormald.overview: A Winchester compilation of 1001×1012 in which a mid-tenth-century Old English Bede was continued with a Chronicle, lists and Alfred and Ine's laws probably all copied from the Parker Manuscript (plus an added text on adultery), the Burghal Hidage, verses on the fasts and medical recipes; a third scribe squeezed in a variant text of Æthelstan’s Grately code. Largely burnt in 1731, it is known chiefly from Laurence Nowell’s transcript of 1562 and Wanley’s description. Wormald sees the whole as essentially a historical collection about the English people, probably made in an episcopal setting.
wormald.liebermann_superseded: Liebermann knew Otho only from its burnt fragments (Af–Ine and II As 7–25); Nowell’s 1562 transcript, unknown to him, shows the original held a complete variant Grately code, an added text on adultery (Ymb Æwbricas), the Burghal Hidage and other items (pp. 173–8).
wormald.key_quote: “it would still be true that the Otho manuscript was first and foremost a historical collection” (p. 180)
wormald.doubts: Table 4.1 dates 1001x1015 (checked in image) while the text (p. 173) says 1001×1012 — both are Wormald’s. Wormald cites Ker, Catalogue no. 180, and Gesetze I p. xxxvi. Liebermann’s posited ‘osq’ (common source of Ot and sq for II As) may need reconsidering in the light of Wormald’s ‘variant text’ argument (Wormald does not discuss osq here). GUIDE: the guide could add that the lost contents (Ymb Æwbricas, Burghal Hidage, ‘Seasons of Fasting’, recipes) are known from Nowell’s transcript, BL Add. 43703. The detached king-list leaf (Add. 34652, f. 2) was identified by Ker (p. 173 n. 42).
